verdict.rationale: Lithic provides infrastructure that supports background autonomous decisioning — Authorization Stream Access lets a customer's endpoint make real-time approval decisions on every transaction, Auth Rules run continuously (including shadow-mode/backtesting) without human intervention, and Lithic explicitly markets 'autonomous issuing, payments, and controls for AI-powered workflows' plus an MCP server for AI coding agents. However, these are building blocks for customers to wire up their own automation logic rather than a built-in scheduler/agent-runner within Lithic itself, and the MCP server is framed as an in-editor coding assistant rather than a background autonomous agent. Missing for 10: a first-party autonomous-agent/automation orchestration feature (vs. APIs customers must wrap themselves), and independent/hands-on evidence of an AI agent actually running unattended in production using these hooks.
